body:
## What

`ZipperBase.MapPiece` now returns the original object for any piece, segment or tile with nothing changed beneath it.

Before, `of_segment`, `of_piece` and `of_tile` rebuilt every tile they walked. A projector update away from the caret (`ProjectorPerform.update`, through `fast_local_seg`'s general case) walks the whole zipper, so each one:
- made a full copy of the program, and
- looked like a whole new program to anything downstream that keys on piece identity (`Segment.ptr_eq`).

## Measured

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `dev`: one tile changed in a 2,000-let program, `MapPiece.of_segment` (`HAZEL_BENCH=1`, group `MapPieceIdentity`, 50 updates) | 3.12 ms per update | 1.92 ms per update |
| livelits branch (#2635): a Kids' Choice slider release, headless Firefox, four runs | 1.5–1.7 s | 0.72–0.88 s |

On `dev` the gain is just the copy. Nothing on `dev` re-parses per item yet, so whole-program syntax work after a projector update is unchanged here.

The livelits branch builds terms one top-level item at a time and reuses an item only if its pieces are the same objects (`MakeTerm.Incr`). There, every livelit commit re-parsed all 31 items of Kids' Choice, twice. With this change it re-parses only the item holding the livelit.

## Tests

- New group `MapPieceIdentity`: an update that changes nothing returns the segment itself; with one tile changed, the pieces before it are the same objects. **Both fail without this change.**
- The quick suite (4,320 tests) passes.

Part of hazelgrove/hazel#2609.

commits.messageBody:
MapPiece rebuilt every tile it walked, even with nothing changed beneath
it. A projector update away from the caret (ProjectorPerform.update,
through fast_local_seg's general case) walks the whole zipper, so each one
copied the whole program, and every layer downstream that keys on piece
identity (Segment.ptr_eq) saw a new one.

of_segment, of_piece and of_tile now return the original object when
nothing beneath it changed.

On dev: one tile changed in a 2,000-let program, 3.12 -> 1.92 ms per
update (HAZEL_BENCH=1, MapPieceIdentity). On the livelits branch, whose
term building re-parses only items whose pieces changed (MakeTerm.Incr),
a livelit commit had re-parsed every item; there a Kids' Choice slider
release went from 1.5-1.7 s to 0.72-0.88 s in Firefox.

Tests: MapPieceIdentity -- an update that changes nothing returns the
segment itself, and with one tile changed the pieces before it are the
same objects; both fail without this change. The quick suite (4,320)
passes. Issue #2609.
